intent: Test the turn-authority lever that the Integrator pre-agreed. Keep mass at 0.6 kg and the ±0.045 m five-sensor span, and narrow wheel_track from 0.10 to 0.09 m to raise yaw rate per unit wheel differential. The aim is to bring s-bend and slalom line_loss_events to 0 and hold max_error below about 0.055 m, while checking that oval progress does not fall further.
learning: Iteration 2 showed that reducing mass alone (0.8 to 0.6 kg) left s-bend and slalom line losses at 1.0 and max_error at the 0.06 m limit, and the combined iteration 1 and 2 designs scored below the baseline. Iteration 3 narrows wheel_track to 0.09 m, the untested turn-authority lever, while holding the other geometry fixed. If s-bend and slalom line losses reach 0 but oval progress stays near 0.12, the shortfall is a controller speed issue. If line losses persist at 1 with max_error at the limit, the geometry has reached its turn-authority range and the next gains must come from the controller.
rationale: Iteration 2 scored 54.1, below the baseline's 62.3, so neither the iteration 1 nor the iteration 2 design has beaten the baseline. Mass 0.8 to 0.6 kg, with the ±0.045 m sensor span and 0.10 m track, left the s-bend and slalom unchanged: line_loss_events stayed at 1.0 and max_error stayed at 0.061 to 0.063 m, just past the 0.06 m off-track limit. Oval line losses fell to 0.35 and the oval progress stayed near 0.12. So the 0.6 kg mass did not give the turn authority the robot needs on the tighter bends. The Integrator's pre-agreed rule applies: with mass 0.6 kg, line losses still at 1 and max_error at the limit, narrow wheel_track to 0.09 m. I keep mass 0.6 kg and the ±0.045 m sensor span, since the oval loss reduction is evidence that the wider reach helps, and I change only wheel_track. I also note the oval progress drop from 0.175 to 0.121 appeared in iteration 1, when wheel_track was first narrowed together with the sensors. Iteration 2 kept the 0.10 m track and progress stayed low, so the track width is a possible cause of the progress loss. A further narrowing could make that worse, so the next race must read oval progress alongside s-bend and slalom line losses. Expected result: s-bend and slalom line_loss_events fall toward 0 and max_error drops below about 0.055 m. If progress falls below 0.12 on oval, the next step is a controller speed change or a return to a wider track, not more narrowing.
